sections.overview: This large predatory sea snail is common in cold North Atlantic waters; French names include buccin commun, bulot and bourgot.
sections.identification: Its heavy shell has a pointed spire, seven or eight rounded whorls, spiral ridges and a short siphonal canal; colour varies geographically.
sections.habitat: It inhabits mud, sand, gravel and rocky seabeds from the shore to deeper shelf waters, and can partly bury itself in soft sediment.
sections.diet: It scavenges dead animals and preys on worms and other bottom invertebrates, detecting food through chemical traces in water.
sections.behavior: Adults move slowly, often partly buried with the siphon exposed, but crawl toward food or away from disturbance.
sections.reproduction: Sexes are separate and fertilization internal; females attach egg capsules to firm objects, and young hatch without a planktonic larval stage.
sections.ecology: Buccinum includes other northern whelks; several congeners occur in the Gulf of St Lawrence, so “whelk” alone may not identify one species.
sections.conservation: Slow growth, late maturity and low mobility make local populations vulnerable to concentrated fishing; management rules vary regionally.
